evidence.note: Measured and cited per-file pass counts (i32.json 376/459 with 83 assert_invalid fails; simd_const 240/445 with 205 fails) and categorized remaining work into validation vs SIMD-execution vs unknown-opcode buckets — a coarse but real sense of what remains.

Attempted the full aggregate run_tests suite but it never completed successfully; the agent never obtained an overall score or a concrete numeric gap to 1.0, and only ever sampled two of many test files.

For ~190 steps the terminal was stuck and the agent repeated the identical stale figures (376/459, 240/445) dozens of times without re-measuring — no updated pass counts, no per-family checklist, no detection that its progress picture had frozen; the same status is restated on nearly every step.

Repeated 'Submit: Mark task complete' attempts and endless restatements of the same known-failure list show it knew work remained but had no evolving ledger of done/remaining/blocked families across the opcode surface.

reasoning: The agent showed a rough mental model of progress — it knew two file-level pass counts and named broad remaining categories — but never maintained a per-family checklist, never updated its counts as work progressed, and only measured 2 of many test files. For the majority of the horizon it recited the same frozen numbers without re-running tests or noticing its picture was stale, matching the '3' anchor (rough sense, no living checklist) rather than the '5' (maintained, updated family checklist with current counts).
